text:
The clearest symptom is f0 = 26.6 MHz against a 25.2–30.8 Hz target, roughly 10⁶× too high. The passive network explains this: for the MFB-style bandpass formed by R1, R2, R3, C1 and C2, the values in the netlist give f0 ≈ 1/(2π·√(R·R·C1·C2)) ≈ 26 MHz, which matches the simulation. The op-amp, bias, and Cd/Rd elements don't set f0 in this way, so the fault is most likely in the frequency-setting passives. I can't pin down the exact element from these numbers alone, so this ranking is a best estimate, not a confirmed diagnosis. A single-element error that large would need a unit or scaling slip of about 10¹² in an RC product, and I haven't verified that against the original design or run a simulation.

{"ranking": ["C1", "C2", "R3"], "fault": "Frequency-setting passive corrupted by a large scaling/unit error (about 10^12 in the RC product), pushing f0 from ~28 Hz to ~26.6 MHz. C1 (5.487e-13 F, the a-to-vout feedback cap) is the most likely culprit; verify by comparing against the nominal design value and re-simulating f0."}
